A_core_direct_lifespan.title: Changes in the gut microbiome and fermentation products concurrent with enhanced longevity in acarbose-treated mice.
evidence_quotes: we compared the fecal microbiome of mice treated with acarbose to control mice at three independent study sites.
Across all three sites, ACA increased the median male survival of the under- lying study population by 17% from 830 to 975 days (log-rank test P < 0.001, see Fig. 1).

B_disease_model_survival.title: Acarbose suppresses symptoms of mitochondrial disease in a mouse model of Leigh syndrome.
evidence_quotes: Here we show that another drug that extends lifespan and delays normative ageing in mice, acarbose, also suppresses symptoms of disease and improves survival of Ndufs4 −/− mice.
Furthermore, rapamycin and acarbose have additive effects in delaying neurological symptoms and increasing maximum lifespan in Ndufs4 −/− mice.

C_secondary_contextual.title: Lifespan-extending interventions induce consistent patterns of fatty acid oxidation in mouse livers.
evidence_quotes: Differential Rank Conservation (DIRAC) analyses of mouse liver proteomics and transcriptomics data show that mechanistically distinct lifespan-extending interventions (acarbose, 17α-estradiol, rapamycin, and calorie restriction) generally tighten the regulation of biological modules.
ACA treatment has been shown to extend lifespan in male mice more than in female mice
